- Moods map as the contract says (date -> Incontro/Harvest for dinner, Kaia's/Rancho for the nightcap; group -> private_dining plus Kaia's; solo -> full_bar plus the bar-forward three; show -> one late stop). - Explainability: every score line carries a weight and a sentence built from real data (service_notes, nightcap.text, late_night.text, tags, desserts, cuisine, posted closing times). stop.reasons is that list sorted best-first; reasons[0] is the paragraph under the name.
- Graceful degrade: if no kitchen has a full dinner runway, it returns the best single stop plus a note; if a stop exists but nothing is open at time + 105, it returns one stop plus a note. Notes are capped at three and name the actual closures ("Incontro is closed Mondays.", "Kaia's closes at 9 PM on Mondays.").

TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS BEYOND THE LITERAL CONTRACT (both add value, both reversible)
1. A restaurant whose bar outlives its kitchen gets a small dinner penalty, because it is worth more as the second stop.
2. If the top-scoring dinner leaves no viable nightcap, the pick trades down by at most 2 points to the next dinner that keeps a second stop alive, and the traded dinner gains the reason "Eating here first keeps Rancho open for the second stop." Without this, 7 PM Monday with no mood picked Rancho (the only late kitchen) and lost the cross-visit entirely; now it returns Harvest at 7 plus Rancho at 8:45. result.notes:
WHAT IT DOES
Single IIFE, classic ES2020 script, 1167 lines, attaches only window.EatSearch and calls init() on load. Zero network calls, no scroll listeners, no inline styles, all markup escaped through a local esc() and every data-driven title run through a highlighter that escapes each slice before wrapping matches in <mark>.

INDEX (built once, lazily, from window.EAT_DATA)
4 restaurants (name, short as name field; cuisine, tags, true-service labels, category alts and the DESIGN.md synonyms as keyword field; description and service_notes as text), every dish, drink and dessert (deduped against dishes), the 10 categories (name, alt, keywords, blurb) and the 7 SERVICE_LABEL services that have no category tile of their own. About 150 entries and two vocabularies.

SCORING
Per query token: best of name x10, keyword x5, text x2, plus 0.6 when it lands in more than one field. Strengths: exact 1, prefix 0.7 to 0.95 (0.45 for a two-letter token), contains 0.5, Damerau-Levenshtein 1 -> 0.5, DL 2 -> 0.35, Dice bigram >= 0.7 -> up to 0.44. Then coverage (0.55 + 0.45 * matched/total), +2.5 when the whole title is inside the query, +4/+2.5 when the query is inside the title, +3*Dice on the whole phrase vs the whole title for misspellings, type prior, EatHours boosts (open +1.2, closing soon -0.8, late_night after 19:00 +1, brunch on weekend mornings +1, the category equivalents at 1.4, sub-entries at 0.6x) and 3 * the learned affinity. "open now" is treated as a clock question and answers only with places that are open.
Cost: about 2 ms per query (each token is compared to the vocabulary once and cached across keystrokes, not once per entry), which fits inside the 40 ms debounce.

UI
Panel renders synchronously, no animation, no transition, nothing added to CSS. Grouped Restaurants / Ways to eat / Dishes and drinks (max 8 rows), each row a .search-item[role=option] inside a role="group", with .thumb (card image, restaurant initial, category letter or a Phosphor icon), .t with <mark>, .s and .k. aria-expanded on the input, .is-open on the .search wrapper, aria-activedescendant follows ArrowUp/ArrowDown (wrapping), Enter activates, Escape and Tab close, click outside closes, panel mousedown is prevented so focus stays in the input. Long blurbs are clipped at their first sentence or clause so a row never grows past two lines.
Empty query: up to 4 recent searches (clock icon) then 4 time-aware starters under "Right now" (at 8 PM exactly Late night, Nightcap, Open now, Dessert), each with a real subtitle and count. Tapping one fills the query and re-runs instantly rather than navigating.
Footer: "Suggestions learn from what you tap, only on this device." plus <kbd>Enter</kbd> to open, <kbd>Esc</kbd> to close.
Placeholder cycles 6 real examples every 3.5 s only while the input is empty, unfocused, the panel is closed and the tab is visible, and never under prefers-reduced-motion (or the site's .reduced class).
/search/ page: reads ?q= on load, re-renders on the same 40 ms debounce, EatDrawer.resultCard for restaurants (with a why line from the matched service note and price plus matched-service chips) and equivalent .result markup for categories (carrying data-drawer-category so app.js opens the drawer), services and menu items. Intro reads "7 results for late night"; an empty query lists the four restaurants ranked by the profile.

INTEGRATION
Satisfies every existing caller: app.js rank(hits, {category}) and learn({type, category|restaurant}), planner.js boost(card.r) and learn(payload). Category activation defers to EatDrawer.showCategory when a #drawer exists (and lets the drawer do its own learn call, so a tap is never counted twice), otherwise navigates to /#c=<slug>. All storage access is wrapped so a private-mode browser degrades to a working, memoryless search.

1. Trigram similarity. CONTRACTS.md says "bigram/trigram similarity"; the build instruction specified Dice over character bigrams, so that is what is implemented (at token level and whole-title level). No trigram pass was added.
2. Damerau-Levenshtein tuning. Distance is never allowed above 2, but distance 2 only counts when the shorter token is at least 6 characters (distance 1 still applies from length 4). Without that, "tiki" matched "Mini" (Mini Donuts) at distance 2 and outranked real hits.
